categories.title: Origins · the wildcat and its cousins
categories.blurb: Every domestic cat descends from the African wildcat; the species beside it show what the family looks like without a fireside.

categories.title: Shorthair · the close-coated breeds
categories.blurb: The classic short coat, from the British cobbiness to the Russian Blue's silver tipping: dense, easy to keep and the base of most modern breeds.

categories.title: Longhair · coats that need a brush
categories.blurb: The Persian line and the northern forest cats: heavy coats, ruffled necks and a build made for cold winters.

categories.title: Oriental · the Siamese family
categories.blurb: One body type in many colours: a long wedge head, a tubular body and a voice that is used constantly.

categories.title: Rex and hairless · coats that broke the rule
categories.blurb: Natural mutations that changed the coat: curls, waves and bare skin, each one a separate breed with its own gene.

categories.title: Hybrids · wild blood at home
categories.blurb: Breeds founded on crosses with wild cats: the Asian leopard cat, the serval and the jungle cat, four to five generations back.

categories.title: Ears and tails · the shape-shifters
categories.blurb: The breeds defined by one changed part: a folded ear, a curled ear, no tail or very short legs, each fixed by a single gene.

categories.title: Rare · breeds few people keep
categories.blurb: Small registries and island populations: the breeds that survived a handful of founders and are still counted in hundreds, not millions.

categories.title: Asia · breeds of the east
categories.blurb: The cats of Thailand, Burma, Iran, Turkey and Japan: pointed coats, silver-blue coats and the breeds that travelled the trade routes first.

categories.title: Africa · breeds of the continent
categories.blurb: The Horn of Africa and the Nile: ticked coats, spots and the wildcat itself, from which every domestic cat on this page descends.

categories.title: Europe · breeds of the north and the islands
categories.blurb: Britain, France, Russia and Scandinavia: dense shorthairs, forest longhairs and the island mutations that gave the rex and the Manx.

categories.title: Americas · breeds of the new world
categories.blurb: The breeds invented in the United States and Canada: the Maine Coon, the Ragdoll, the Sphynx and the wild hybrids of the last fifty years.
